items.title: Centre tells Delhi High Court that Saurav Das' passport has discrepancies, may impact citizenship
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday was informed by the Central government that a look out circular (LOC) has been issued against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Saurav Das, preventing his travel abroad. Appearing for the Centre, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma told Justice Amit Mahajan that the discrepancies pointed out in Das’s passport may also have a bearing on his Indian citizenship. Sharma, assisted by Central Government Standing Counsel (CGSC) Ashish Dixit, stated that the LOC has been issued against Das at the request of Mumbai Police. He said that inquiries were made about Das’ place of birth, schooling, address and parentage because he left the father’s name column blank in his passport. “There are multiple discrepancies so an inquiry is done. Pursuant to the inquiry, on November 23, a show cause notice and advisory were issued at 7:32 PM and 7:56 PM… Assuming he travels abroad and he does not attend the meeting [regarding his passport] or he attends and a discrepancy is found which goes to the very root of the matter. items.title: 10 former CJIs inaugurate India's first Chief Justices of India Museum at OP Jindal Global University
items.summary: On the eve of Constitution Day, 10 former Chief Justices of India came together, in person or virtually, to inaugurate India’s first Chief Justices of India Museum at OP Jindal Global University (JGU). Envisioned as “Guardians of the Republic,” the Museum brings judicial history into conversation with art, technology and personal testimony, inviting visitors to explore how justice shapes individual lives and the destiny of a nation. Across five galleries, it features more than 280 busts of Supreme Court judges, models of 25 High Courts, 22 language tapestries, 20 interactive biographical pillars and 20 defining judgments, alongside a holographic courtroom and an extensive collection of artworks, sculptures and installations. The inauguration brought together former Chief Justices MN Venkatachaliah , BN Kirpal , S Rajendra Babu , KG Balakrishnan , P Sathasivam , RM Lodha , Dipak Misra , SA Bobde , UU Lalit and BR Gavai . Hailing the occasion, Naveen Jindal , the Founding Chancellor of JGU said, “The Constitution of India is the enduring foundation of our Republic, embodying the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. items.title: Allahabad High Court verdict denying right to wear hijab in school not a precedent: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently said that the Allahabad High Court's August 21 judgment upholding a school's ban on wearing a hijab in classrooms shall not be treated as a precedent [ Muslim Womens Study Circle vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi made the observation while issuing notice to the State of Uttar Pradesh on a an appeal challenging the High Court verdict. The Court tagged the matter with the pending batch of appeals arising out of the Karnataka hijab ban case . "Permission to file the petition is granted. Issue notice. Tag with Civil Appeal No. 7095/2022 and this judgment shall not be treated as precedent," the Bench recorded in its November 20 order. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi The appeal before the apex court was filed against the High Court's August 21 judgment, which had upheld a school's classroom ban on headscarves while ruling that wearing a hijab is not an essential religious practice in Islam. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday closed mediation proceedings between Rani Kapur and her daughter-in-law Priya Sachdev Kapur after efforts to resolve the dispute over late industrialist Sunjay Kapur's family trust failed. [Rani Kapur Vs Priya Sachdeva Kapur] A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran was informed that Rani Kapur had sought ₹6,000 crore to settle her claims against the trust, whose assets were valued by the opposing counsel at around ₹30,000 crore. “One can never force a settlement ,” the Court remarked. The Court indicated that the Delhi High Court should now decide the pending application seeking preservation of the trust's assets in a time-bound manner. The dispute concerns the validity of the RK Family Trust, which holds substantial wealth associated with the Sona Group. Sunjay Kapur, the former chairman of auto components major Sona Comstar, died in June 2025. items.title: Are those who turned innocent people into Naxals behind bars? President Droupadi Murmu asks
items.summary: President Droupadi Murmu on Thursday said those surrendering as Naxals had been brainwashed and drawn into the movement, and called for efforts to understand why innocent people were made to become Naxals. Speaking at the Constitution Day celebrations at the Supreme Court of India, Murmu said the country has become Naxal-free and that those who had surrendered should be treated with compassion. "मैं धन्यवाद देना चाहती हूँ सरकार को। आज पूरा देश नक्सल मुक्त हो गया है। जो नक्सल सरेंडर कर रहे थे, मैं उनके चेहरे देख रही थी। उनका मासूम चेहरा देखकर मुझे नहीं लगता कि ये नक्सल हैं। इन्हें नक्सल बनाया गया है। पता नहीं, जिन लोगों ने इन्हें बनाया है, वे अंदर हैं कि नहीं। लेकिन जिन लोगों को जबरदस्ती नक्सल बनाया गया है, वे लोग अंदर हैं। उसके ऊपर थोड़ा काम करना चाहिए, क्योंकि वे लोग मासूम हैं।" said Murmu. items.title: Tata Trusts move Bombay High Court against resolution appointing N Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman
items.summary: The corporate tussle at Tata Sons Limited has formally reached the judiciary, with Tata Trusts approaching the Bombay High Court today with two suits. The matter was mentioned before Justice Arif S Doctor , who recused from hearing the suit. Justice Arif Doctor The petition was then mentioned before Justice Abhay Ahuja , who has granted hearing for tomorrow. Justice Abhay Ahuja Tata Trusts has challenged the September 17 board resolution which reappointed N Chandrasekaran as the executive chairman of Tata Sons and Tata Group. On September 17, the Tata Sons board had passed a resolution approving a fresh five-year term for Chandrasekaran. The resolution was passed 4:1. Directors Venu Srinivasan, Harish Manwani, Anita M George and Saurabh Agrawal voted in favour. Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata voted against; Chandrasekaran abstained. Tata Trusts has sought a declaration that the resolution is ultra vires the Articles of Association, hence null and void. items.title: Thiruparankundram and Hindutva | The men claiming to know what's best for women | South Central 103
items.summary: What happens when a centuries-old religious dispute becomes a political flashpoint? How has the controversy over lighting a lamp atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai been used to fuel communal tensions in Tamil Nadu? Listen and follow on YouTube Listen and follow on Apple Listen and follow on Spotify In this week's South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna are joined by The News Minute's Executive Editor Sudipto Mondal and reporter Azeefa Fathima to examine the growing controversy surrounding Thiruparankundram hill. The discussion traces the dispute back to the 19th century, exploring its history, the hill's significance to Hindus, Muslims and Jains, and how successive governments have handled the conflict. The conversation looks at a Tamil Nadu government archaeological survey that identified the disputed pillar as a British-era triangulation marker, rather than a lamp pillar. Sudipto discusses how the dispute has evolved over more than a century, the role of successive governments and the ways in which Hindutva politics has attempted to turn a shared religious space into a site of communal mobilisation.
